items.title: feat: support GLM5.2 LoRA training and checkpoint correctness
items.bodyExcerpt:
## What this PR does / why we need it?


 完善 GLM5.2 原生 LoRA 训练的参数结构、并行梯度处理、checkpoint 保存与加载，以及独立 A 的 HF 合并导出能力。

  主要修改：

  - 支持 Q/KV 独立 A：在原生 PEFT LoRA 中为 Q、KV 分别维护可训练的 A 矩阵，保留原有 B 的输出分块。新增参数在 DDP 和优化器初始化前注册，克隆初值不额外消耗随机数。
  - 修正专家并行梯度：补齐专家 LoRA 参数的 expert-DP 属性，区分 ETP 复制参数与分片参数，对复制参数累加各特征分片产生的梯度。
  - 补齐 MLA 的 TP 输入梯度：在 absorb 路径中保留 SP gather 行为，并为非 SP 的 TP 场景补充 KV 输入梯度求和。
  - 修正非均匀 PP 层号：补齐新版 Megatron 全局层偏移函数的注册，避免非均匀分层时出现层编号及 DSA 共享关系错位。
  - 完善 checkpoint 正确性：LoRA checkpoint 保留训练期间更新的 router bias；首次加载底座及 adapter 重载前将对应 buffer 保持为 FP32，避免复制过程中的精度损失；修复 swap optimizer 与禁用 Gloo 的分布式 Adam 保存路径组合下读取已释放设备存储的问题。
  - 支持独立 A 的 HF 合并导出：对 Q、KV 输出行分别使用对应的 A 矩阵计算 LoRA 增量，并支持普通线性层及 grouped 专家权重合并。补充形状、配置、非有限值及未处理 LoRA 参数检查；逐层导出采用 mmap 读取和按层释放，降低内存峰值。

  训练侧适配通过 MindSpeed-LLM 的 feature 机制及模型构建流程接入，导出修改位于 checkpoint 转换模块，无需修改 MindSpeed 或 Megatron-LM 源文件。CP 序列布局、标签对齐及 aux loss 适配单独处理，不包含在本 PR 中。

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

  主要包括以下变化：

  - 新增可选参数 --lora-qkv-independent-a，默认关闭。开启后，Q/KV 使用初值相同但独立训练的 A 矩阵；要求 LoRA targets 包含 linear_qkv，并配置 --mla-mm-split 和 --q-lora-rank。
  - 本 PR 中独立 Q/KV A 暂要求 context_parallel_size=1；开启该功能时使用 CP>1 会明确报错，待后续 CP 适配补齐。这一限制不针对原有共享 A 路线。
  - 独立 A 当前支持普通、未融合的单 adapter LoRA，不支持 DoRA 或训练层的 PEFT 在线 adapter merge；支持通过 checkpoint 转换器离线合并并导出 HF 权重。
  - 开启独立 A 后，adapter checkpoint 新增 lora_A_kv 参数，加载时需使用匹配配置。启用 expert bias 时，LoRA checkpoint 同时保存 router bias。
  - HF 合并导出支持底座与 adapter 分开加载，以及统一 checkpoint 路径。需使用匹配的 LoRA rank、alpha 和权重布局；检测到不兼容或遗漏参数时明确报错。
  - 并行梯度和 checkpoint 修复在对应配置下生效，可能改变原错误路径下的参数更新或加载结果；关闭独立 A 开关不会关闭这些正确性修复。

items.title: [RFC] LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training
items.bodyExcerpt:
# [RFC] LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training

## Problem

RL + LoRA workflows have three vLLM-side issues:

1. **sleep/wake crash**: Level-2 sleep with `enable_lora=True` crashes with KeyError — LoRA adapter parameters are not in cumem's tag set ([#39934](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39934))
2. **Adapter-only sync missing**: frameworks must merge LoRA → send full weights → unmerge. Adapter-only sync (send only LoRA delta, load via vLLM's LoRA serving) would eliminate the merge round-trip ([trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975))
3. **LoRA + MoE mismatch**: logprob divergence between training and inference grows with LoRA rank on MoE models (Qwen3.6, GLM-4.7-Flash) ([SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776))

## Downstream demand

- [trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975): Adapter-only vLLM LoRA sync for GRPO/AsyncGRPO
- [SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776): LoRA + MoE inference mismatch investigation
- [verl#6782](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/6782): Qwen3.5-27B LoRA GRPO — vLLM never emits EOS with rank=64

## Exit criterion

- sleep/wake + LoRA (#39934) no longer crashes
- Adapter-only sync path available (no full-weight merge required)

## Feedback Period

Two weeks from posting.

items.title: [Bug]: Native CPU offloading can compute inconsistent num_cpu_blocks across PP ranks
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

Hardware: 4 × NVIDIA B300, single-node server
Architecture: x86_64
vLLM: 0.26.0 container for runtime reproduction; upstream main for the proposed fix
torch: 2.11.0+cu130
CUDA: 13.0, NVIDIA driver 580.126.20
Distributed executor: mp, --pipeline-parallel-size 4, --tensor-parallel-size 1
KV offloading: native CPU offloading via OffloadingConnector, prefix caching enabled, no SSD offloading

Model
GLM-5.2-NVFP4

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Native CPU offloading can compute inconsistent CPU cache block counts across pipeline-parallel ranks.
A proposed fix is available in #50653

 ## Problem
In pipeline parallelism, each worker's `KVCacheConfig` only contains the layers owned by that worker's PP stage. Native CPU offloading derives its CPU cache capacity from the local worker KV cache tensors.

 When different PP stages own different numbers or types of layers, the per-worker KV bytes per block can differ. As a result, the scheduler and workers can compute different `num_cpu_blocks`.

The scheduler uses the first worker's KV cache config, while workers build offloading specs from their local configs. If the scheduler-side CPU block count is larger than a worker's local CPU buffer capacity, offloaded block IDs can exceed that worker's allocated CPU cache range.

 ## Example

 For a model with 8 layers, `pipeline_parallel_size=2`, `tensor_parallel_size=1`:

  ```text
  PP stage 0: 5 FullAttention layers
  PP stage 1: 3 FullAttention layers

  page_size_per_layer = 65536 bytes
  num_gpu_blocks = 1000
  cpu_bytes_to_use = 10 GiB
  ```
  Before the fix:
  ```text
  Scheduler / PP stage 0:
  total_gpu_kv_bytes = 5 * 65536 * 1000
  kv_bytes_per_block = 327680
  num_cpu_blocks = 32768

  Worker / PP stage 1:
  total_gpu_kv_bytes = 3 * 65536 * 1000
  kv_bytes_per_block = 196608
  num_cpu_blocks = 54613
  ```
 This means different PP ranks can allocate different CPU offload buffer sizes for the same scheduler-visible CPU block ID space.

items.title: [Bug]: minimax_m2 / glm47_moe / deepseek_v4 arg converters drop the last parameter when the model omits the closing tag (same class as #57699)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

- vLLM main (probed 2026-09-20; minimax_m2.py @ 24bfbd5d, deepseek_v4.py @ 39e33db7)
- Parser-only bug: reproduction needs no GPU, no model, no server.

### Describe the bug

#57699 describes a bug class for qwen3: when the model closes the tool call **without closing the last parameter tag**, the trailing value is dropped by the final (partial=False) conversion. #57707 fixes qwen3 only - but the same structure exists in three other converters, none of which are covered by that PR:

**1. minimax_m2 - vllm/parser/minimax_m2.py `_minimax_m2_arg_converter`**

`_PARAM_RE` only ends a value at the closing parameter tag or at the next parameter open tag. The trailing `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` extraction runs only under `if partial:`, so the final conversion drops the last parameter. With `stream_arg_deltas=True`, the streamed partial conversions have already emitted the value, and the flush at tool-call end produces a shorter JSON - the same client-visible divergence as #57699.

Model output:

```
<minimax:tool_call><invoke name="get_weather">
<parameter name="city">Seattle</parameter>
<parameter name="unit">celsius
</invoke></minimax:tool_call>

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offloading] Fix CPU offload block count mismatch across PP ranks
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation

Native CPU offloading computes CPU cache capacity from each worker's KV cache tensors. Under pipeline parallelism, workers may own different numbers or types of layers, so different PP ranks can derive different CPU offload block counts.

The scheduler uses the first worker's KV cache config, while workers build offloading specs from their local configs. If the scheduler-side CPU block count is larger than a worker's local CPU buffer capacity, offloaded block IDs can exceed that worker's allocated CPU cache range.

### Runtime Validation

  I reproduced the issue with vLLM v0.26.0 using:

  - Model: `GLM-5.2-NVFP4`
  - `pipeline_parallel_size=4`
  - `tensor_parallel_size=1`
  - Native CPU offloading via `OffloadingConnector`
  - Prefix caching enabled
  - No SSD offloading

  Before the fix, different PP ranks computed different CPU offload block counts from their local KV cache tensors:

  ```text
  scheduler/rank0 CPU num_blocks: 35341
  worker/rank0 CPU num_blocks: 35341
  worker/rank1 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank2 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank3 CPU num_blocks: 36561
  ```
  This confirms the mismatch. Since the scheduler allocates CPU block IDs based on its own CPU block count, rank1/rank2 only had capacity for 34435 blocks while the scheduler could allocate IDs up to 35340. Those IDs would be outside rank1/rank2's CPU buffer range.

  After applying the fix, all PP ranks used the same unified minimum CPU block count:
  ```text
  scheduler CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank0 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank1 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank2 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank3 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  ```
  The fixed server also started successfully and returned successful responses:

  GET /health -> 200
  POST /v1/completions -> 200

  ### Proposed Changes

  - Add `num_cpu_blocks` to `KVCacheConfig` and `OffloadingConfig`.
  - Compute CPU offload block capacity for every worker KV

## Purpose

Fixes #54744.

With `--reasoning-parser glm45`/`glm47`, passing `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` (or `thinking: false`) disables the parser's reasoning extraction. For GLM-4.5/4.6 that is correct, because their templates honor the kwarg and the model emits no think block. GLM-5.3-family templates read neither kwarg, so the model thinks unconditionally, and the raw scratchpad plus a dangling `</think>` lands in `message.content`:

```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": "Simple question.</think>2 + 2 = **4**\n\n..."}

The request-scoped engine keeps the unarmed config, so the streaming and id-space paths (`is_reasoning_end`, `extract_content_ids`) are untouched.

Auto-detection there would require buffering content for models that legitimately disabled thinking, which is worse than the leak. Operators hitting this should drop the ignored kwarg for GLM-5.3 deployments; the non-streaming leak this PR closes is the verified repro from the issue.

items.title: [Kernel] persistent_topk: deterministic select, faster than the exact-topk workaround
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A deterministic `persistent_topk` (the QSA / sparse-indexer block selection,
`csrc/libtorch_stable/persistent_topk.cuh`) that is **also faster than the exact-topk workaround**
people currently reach for. The kernel returns a different result for identical inputs from call to
call: the **order** always varies, and when more keys share the threshold value than the candidate
buffers hold, the selected **set** varies too. Cause: output slots are handed out by `atomicAdd` in
thread-arrival order, and exact-key ties at the last radix round are taken first-come.

### Motivation update (2026-09-21) — read this before the original framing below

This PR was opened as a determinism fix. **On the evidence since, that framing overstates the
case, and I am restating it rather than leaving the body arguing something the threads have
undermined.** Three independent readings:

1. **Ours.** We censused the top-k boundary on real traffic: **0 ties at the k-th value across 6,192
   selecting rows** at 16k context ([09-12](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55122#issuecomment-5602743511)).
   93 % of rows had fewer visible blocks than k, so selection was a no-op.
2. **The reporter of #51782.** @xueyangcs states the HPC-Ops TopK contract is **set-exact only** —
   with ties, any valid top-k set is permitted; set-stability was never guaranteed
   ([#51782, 09-09](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51782)).
3. **An independent field report.** @NNNtrance replaced the selection with an exact `torch.topk` on

   ([#51782, 09-12](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51782)).

traffic that motivated it.** What survives is the performance argument, which is independently

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Stop dummy draft decode steps from writing KV through stale block-table rows
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix a KV-cache corruption in Model Runner V2 speculative decoding under data parallelism: an idle DP rank's dummy batch runs the drafter's multi-step decode, which computes real slot mappings through the *persistent* per-slot block tables using `idx_mapping = arange(num_reqs)` (real request-state slots whose rows are stale), and writes drafter-layer K/V into offsets `1..k-1` of the first block of whatever request last occupied those slots. Those blocks are typically already registered in the prefix cache, so every later request that hits them reads corrupted drafter K/V while the target model's K/V stays intact.

Observed on GLM-5.2 (glm_moe_dsa, MTP k=5, DP=4 EP, prefix caching) as a per-request, exactly-zero MTP acceptance (`p0 = 0.0000`, `acc_len = 1.0`, `drafts == max_tokens`) that latches onto a conversation and disappears after `POST /reset_prefix_cache`; the poisoned rows were NaN (fp8 `0x7F`) in `model.layers.78.self_attn.attn`, with the target layers and indexer cache of the same block clean. On current main the same stale write still happens on every idle step (the written values happen to be finite there, so acceptance is unaffected), i.e. the write path is latent.

#49757 protected the read side (`get_dummy_block_tables` zeroes `input_block_tables`) and the target's dummy slot mappings are PAD (`prepare_dummy_attn`), but `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` reads `block_table_ptrs` (the persistent tables), which neither protection covers.

## Fix

- `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel`: a row with `idx_mapping < 0` (dummy or CUDA-graph padding request) emits `PAD_SLOT_ID` and never dereferences a negative block-table row.

## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash carries a kpool-tail scratch group (`KpoolTailSpec`, `prefix_cacheable=False`, `block_size=index_kpool=4`) next to prefix-cacheable groups that hash at 1152 tokens on this box (MLA 1152, 4× Mamba 1152 in `align` mode). Core (`resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes`, `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`, `KVCacheManager`) and the `MooncakeStore connector` already skip such groups. `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` did not, and treated every KV cache group as offloadable:

- `_select_eager_blocks_to_store` views the request hashes at each group's block size to build `BlockStored` metadata. For the tail group that is `resolve_block_hashes(hashes, hash_block_size=1152, block_size=4)`, which trips the divisibility assert as soon as `--kv-events-config` enables KV cache events. The engine dies on the first prefill store.
- `update_state_after_alloc` maps external (CPU-hit) tokens onto the scratch group and asserts alignment against its block size, although the coordinator never returns hit blocks for it.

This PR records which groups take part in offloading (`prefix_cacheable`) and skips the rest in eager store selection and in load pairing. Scratch blocks never carry a hash, so nothing is stored or loaded for them either way; the scratch slot in the per-group hit tuple stays empty, exactly as the coordinator leaves it.


## Duplication check

Two open PRs touch the same code path: #55033 (draft since 2026-09-02, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA ring, also adjusts `_estimate_lazy_target_blocks`) and #56404 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, gates `resolve_block_hashes` in the store path only, currently conflicting). items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix silent indexer-cache corruption for GLM-5.3-Flash on NVIDIA: the kpool prefill tail-seed kernel addresses tail blocks with a dense stride while the tail cache is stored with the indexer's padded block stride.

**How the tail cache is laid out.** `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` pads the `KpoolTailSpec` page to the indexer page (`page_size_padded = idx_page`; 38016 B for the default `block_size=1152`: 288 pool rows x 132 B), and `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` places every indexer layer's tail tensor at the *same offset* as that layer's indexer tensor with `block_stride = idx_page`. Tail block `b` is therefore the first 2048 B (`[2, kpool=4, 128]` bf16) of indexer block `b`; the two never collide because both groups draw distinct block ids from one pool. `create_kv_cache_views` builds the view with `as_strided`, so `tail_kv_cache.stride(0) == 19008` elements instead of the dense 1024.

**The bug.** `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/kpool_compress.py` computed

```python
base = (blk * 2 * KPOOL + t % KPOOL) * HEAD_DIM   # dense 2048 B block stride
```

so for every prefill it (a) left the request's own tail block unseeded and (b) wrote 2048 B of raw bf16 K / gate rows at byte `blk * 2048` of the layer's indexer region, i.e. into indexer block `blk * 2048 // 38016` at offset `blk * 2048 % 38016` — fp8 key rows or the fp32 scale region of whatever request owns that block. The decode kernel (`TAIL_BLOCK_ELEMS` / `KPOOL_HEAD`) and the AMD seed kernel already address the tail through `stride(0)` / `stride(1)`; only the NVIDIA seed kernel did not, and the existing regression test for exactly this layout was `skipif(not is_rocm)`.

**Why it shows up as "the cached system prompt is broken".** Only indexer blocks with id below `num_blocks * 2048 / 38016` (~5% of the pool) can be hit, and those are the ids handed out first after startup, i.e. the blocks of the first prefix-cached prompt, typically a long-lived system prompt. ## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash sparse-MLA models keep a one-block-per-request circular tail cache (kpool). Every decode step — twice per step with MTP, once for the target model and once for the drafter — `KpoolTailMetadataBuilder.build()` maps each token to its request's tail ring with a chain of small torch ops (`arange` + `searchsorted` + `clamp` + `index_select` + `remainder` + `copy_`): 12 kernel launches and ~250 us of CPU enqueue time per build.

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Cap the DynamicVideoBackend sampling fps
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`DynamicVideoBackend` (`vllm/multimodal/video.py`, registered as `opencv_dynamic`)
sizes its frame-candidate walk directly from the request-supplied `fps`, so the
amount of work is unbounded by anything in the video:

```python
fps = target.fps
...
if duration <= max_duration:
    n = int(math.floor(duration * fps))
    frame_indices_list = sorted(
        {min(max_frame_idx, math.ceil(i / fps * original_fps)) for i in range(n)}
    )
```

`n` scales with `fps`, but the *result* does not: the largest index reachable is
`duration * original_fps` regardless, and the set deduplicates at the end. So a
large `fps` buys nothing and costs CPU linearly.

This applies the same clamp the sibling backends in this file already use —
`_MAX_FPS: ClassVar[int] = 30` plus `fps = min(target.fps, cls._MAX_FPS)`, which
is verbatim what `QwenVLVideoBackend` (`:362`/`:373`, from the merged #56729) and
`GLMGAVideoBackend` (`:812`/`:839`) do.

`fps` is request-controlled through `media_io_kwargs`, and nothing strips it for
this backend:

1. `opencv_dynamic` is registered with `video_processor="Glm4vVideoProcessor"`,

Offline `LLM.generate` with Whisper and an audio clip longer than 30 s kills the engine on main and on v0.29.0:

items.title: [Bugfix][Determinism] Refuse batch-invariant mode on the sparse indexer
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` looks like it works on DSA / sparse-indexer models. It
does not: the indexer's top-k has no batch-invariant backend, so which keys a
row attends to can change with the rest of the batch.

Every path is batch-dependent:

| backend | what makes it batch-dependent |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | switches kernels at `AUTO_COOPERATIVE_MAX_ROWS` (64) rows — `indexer_topk.py:_resolve_auto` |
| `per_row` | picks among three algorithms from the **padded column count**, i.e. the batch's longest sequence (`sampler.cu`, `kSortingAlgorithmThreshold` / `kSplitWorkThreshold`); on gfx950 it also splits a row across blocks by row count |
| `persistent` | sizes its cooperative launch from occupancy and the batch's max sequence length, and falls back to `per_row` when the launch does not fit (`topk.cu`) |
| `cooperative` | only applicable under the 64-row cap, so it is by definition batch-conditional |

None of this changes the logits. It changes tie-breaking and therefore the
selection — and a different sparse selection is a different forward pass, not a
rounding difference.
